name: Lithium niobate
equilibrium_context: Strong ferroelectric, Curie temperature about 1480 K, large spontaneous polarization

driven_states.emergent_property: Resonant excitation of a high-frequency auxiliary phonon mode leads, via strong anharmonic coupling, to a directional displacement along the ferroelectric mode; the polarization is transiently reversed, visible as a sign change of the phase-resolved second harmonic.

drive.driven_mode: highest A1 mode, 19 THz, anharmonically coupled to the soft A1 mode

driven_states.source: Mankowsky, von Hoegen, Foerst & Cavalleri, Phys. Rev. Lett. 118, 197601 (2017), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.118.197601
driven_states.caveat: A transient ionic displacement, not remanent domain switching. After a few picoseconds the polarization returns to its initial state. The interpretation as a genuine reversal rests on the modeling of the sign of the second harmonic.

threshold.quantity: sign reversal only above a critical excitation amplitude

sources: Mankowsky et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 118, 197601 (2017), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.118.197601

provenance.notes: Literature search and field extraction by AI agents under the direction of D. Leonforte; every numerical value and citation checked against the cited work and every DOI verified. Not reviewed by a domain expert. Corrections are welcome and are the intended path to improvement.
